payload.goal: A session serves the network of threads around its task, not one log: task text, blocked notes, next actions and note prose become citation sources under the existing closed grammar; a typed waits_on link names what a blocked task waits on and the fold reports when the target has since moved; repo-memory lines become nodes so M<n> resolves; the SessionStart digest carries a bounded one-hop travel block rendered from existing projection fields (byte-stable, Rust-renderable, never generated prose); and an on-demand answer packet composes ranked, id-cited atoms for a question. Deterministic throughout, zero model calls; judge-ranked selection is typed-judge's job. Design in roadmap-h2 notes 01M2ZDKDRACY87BA26VWN825VP and 01M2ZESQFZWVM8TYHXG19YYVZN. Parked until taken up.

payload.text:
READY SKELETON (2026-09-20) — turn into a plan with one sofar_update_plan call when taken up. Contract first (rust-core D1): every render here gets SPEC text and golden fixtures before code.
Phase 1 — Citation sources. 1.1 SPEC: extend §Record graph `cites` sources to task_added/plan_updated task text, task_status_changed notes, session_ended next_action, note_added prose; same closed grammar, sourcing event id on the edge. 1.2 Implement in the index pass (record-index cursors), retroactive; tests over this repo's record. 1.3 `sofar find` / reach rows show the new edge sources.
Phase 2 — waits_on. 2.1 Schema (packages/schema only): optional `waits_on` handle list on task_status_changed(blocked) and on plan tasks. 2.2 Fold: a blocked task resolves its targets against the target log and reports moved/resolved since (decision superseded, task done, initiative closed). 2.3 MCP: sofar_update_task accepts waits_on; digest renders "blocked on X — moved 3d ago".
Phase 3 — Memory nodes. 3.1 Mint nodes for repo.md M<n> lines so the grammar resolves them (lifts the record-citations restriction). 3.2 Adjacency and reach include memory nodes.
Phase 4 — Digest travel block. 4.1 SPEC + fixtures: from the next task only, 1 hop over cites, 2 over waits_on; per-target render from projection fields (initiative: status/next action/latest decision; decision: chose line + date; task: id/status/note tail; memory: line); cap 6 targets / 600 chars; tail "…and N more — sofar find <seed>". 4.2 Implement TS; index-read only, inside the 100 ms hook budget. 4.3 Rust parity after rust-core 2.4.
Phase 5 — Answer packets. 5.1 `sofar_ask`/find compose mode: gather (BM25 + traversal), deterministic order (waits_on, cites, adjacency), clip at budget with ids kept, "changed since" line. 5.2 Judge-ranked variant delegated to typed-judge C1/D2.
Phase 6 — Proof. 6.1 Bench: cross-record resume scenario, tokens and turns before/after (predictions in typed-judge note 01M2ZV3KEV2XA467NW7TN6WYWZ).

payload.text: PLANNING RESEARCH (2026-09-29). Internal: hot-path today (team100 gate 226d1a3d v3) Rust session-start warm 7.8ms/19MB, 19.6ms/95MB; TS repo 75ms warm, 141ms cold (HOTPATH.md). Digest 6k cap; ~1.67k tokens vs ~15k full state. Constraints found: reach code banned from hook bundles (graph-hotpath.test.ts:177-220); reach has no Rust reader and is refreshed only by find; cites edges today are decision-only and D<n>-only in reach; task_status_changed note is free text (fold.ts blockNotes); schema field text feeds the fingerprint, so any schema change invalidates snapshot/checkpoint/digest caches once. Rejected elsewhere, do not re-propose: embeddings/LLM extraction (felt-cost D3), resident daemon (rust-core D39/D42), pointer-only disclosure (token-optimization D6/D7), two-hop joins through hub files (record-index D9), in-band "+N more" strings (record-graph D6). External: beads has 19 dep types but only blocks/parent-child/conditional-blocks/waits-for gate readiness, so we use one readiness predicate; Graphiti uses bi-temporal validity + hop-distance rerank (our analogue: supersedes/until events), ~1.6k vs 115k tokens; Letta uses fixed per-block char limits; aider repo-map damps hub identifiers (x0.1) and boosts focus items, and at one hop PPR reduces to focus-term scoring, so no PageRank needed. Lever ranking: 1 write-time links tier, 2 readiness-gated inclusion, 3 fixed carve + numeric omitted, 4 supersession filter before ranking, 5 hub damping, 6 focus ranking, 7 dedupe vs rendered rules/memory, 8 check-before-parse typed reader.
